You make me Fool for Company: Fie, Soldiers,
My Soldiers too, and play these Tricks. What's he there?
Sure I have seen his Face too; yes, most certain
I have a Son, but I hope he is not here now,
Would much resemble this Man, wondrous near him,
Just of his height and making too; you seem a Leader.

speeches.speaker: The.
verse: Good Sir, do not shame me more: I know your Anger,
And less than Death I look not for.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: You shall be my Charge, Sir, it seems you want Foes,
When you would make your Friends your Enemies:
A running Blood you have, but I shall cure you.

speeches.speaker: Bur.
verse: Good Sir —

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: No more, good Lord: beat forward, Soldiers:
And you, march in the Rear, you have lost your Places.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: You shall not be thus sullen still, with me, Sister,
You do the most unnobly to be angry;
For as I have a Soul, I never touch'd her,
I never yet knew one unchast Thought in her:
I must confess I lov'd her; as who would not?
I must confess I doated on her strangely,
I offer'd, all; yet so strong was her Honour,
So fortify'd as fair, no Hope could reach her;
And whilst the World beheld this, and confirm'd it,
Why would you be so jealous?

speeches.speaker: Ol.
verse: Good Sir pardon me,
I feel sufficiently my Follies Penance,
And am asham'd, that Shame a thousand Sorrows
Feed on continually. Would I had never seen her,
Or with a clearer Judgment look'd upon her:
She was too good for me, so heavenly good, Sir,
Nothing but Heaven can love that Soul sufficiently,
Where I shall see her once again.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: No more Tears,
If she be within the Dukedom, we'll recover her:
Welcome, Lord Burris, fair News I hope.

speeches.speaker: Bu.
verse: Most fair, Sir,
Without one Drop of Blood these Wars are ended,
The Soldier cool'd again, indeed asham'd, Sir,
And all his Anger ended.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: Where's Lord Archas?

speeches.speaker: Bur.
verse: Not far off, Sir: with him his valiant Son,
Head of this Fire, but now a Prisoner;
And if by your sweet Mercy not prevented,
I fear some fatal Stroke.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: I hear the Drums beat,
Welcome, my worthy Friend.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: Stand where you are, Sir,
Even as you love your Country, move not forward,
Nor plead for Peace till I have done a Justice,
A Justice on this Villain; none of mine now,
A Justice on this Rebel.

speeches.speaker: Hon.
verse: O my Brother.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: This fatal Firebrand —

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: Forget not, old Man,
He is thy Son of thine own Blood.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: In these Veins
No treachery e'er harbour'd yet, no mutiny,
I ne'er gave life to lewd and headstrong Rebels.

speeches.speaker: Duk.
verse: 'Tis his first Fault.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: Not of a thousand Sir,
Or were it so, it is a Fault so mighty.
So strong against the Nature of all Mercy,
His Mother were she living, would not weep for him;
He dare not say he would live.

speeches.speaker: The.
verse: I must not Sir,
Whilst you say it is not fit: your Grace's mercy
Not to my life apply'd, but to my fault Sir,
The World's forgiveness next; last, on my Knees Sir,
I humbly beg,
Do not take from me yet the Name of Father,
Strike me a thousand Blows, but let me dye yours.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: He moves my Heart: I must be suddain with him,
I shall grow faint else, in my Execution;
Come, come Sir, you have seen Death; now meet him bravely.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: Hold, hold I say, a little hold, consider
Thou hast no more Sons, Archas, to inherit thee:

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: Yes Sir, I have another, and a Nobler:
No Treason shall inherit me: young Archas
A Boy, as sweet as young, my Brother breeds him,
My noble Brother Brisky, breeds him nobly,
Him let your favour find: give him your honour.

speeches.speaker: Put.
verse: Thou hast no Child left Ar chas, none to inherit thee
If thou strik'st that stroke now: behold young Archas;
Behold thy Brother here, thou bloody Brother,
As bloody to this Sacrifice as thou art:
Heave up thy Sword, and mine's heav'd up: strike Archas,
And I'll strke too, as suddenly, as deadly:
Have Mercy, and I'll have Mercy: The Duke gives it,
Look upon all these, how they weep it from thee,
Choose quickly, and begin.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: On your Obedience,
On your Allegiance save him.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: Take him to you,
And sirrah, be an honest Man, you have reason:
I thank ye worthy Brother; welcome Child,
Mine one sweet Child.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: Why was this Boy concealed thus?

speeches.speaker: Put.
verse: Your Grace's Pardon:
Fearing the Vow you made against my Brother
And that your Anger would not only light
On him, but find out all his Family,
This Young Boy, to preserve from after danger,
Like a young Wench, hither I brought; my self
In the Habit of an ordinary Captain
Disguis'd, got Entertainment, and serv'd here
That I might still be ready to all Fortunes:
The Boy your Grace took, nobly entertain'd him,
But thought a Girl, Alinda, Madam.

speeches.speaker: Ol.
verse: Stand away,
And let me look upon him.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: My young Mistriss?
This is a strange Metamorphosis, Alinda,

speeches.speaker: Al.
verse: Your Graces humble Servant.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: Come hither Sister:
I dare yet scarce believe mine Eyes? how they view one another?
Dost thou not love this Boy well?

speeches.speaker: Ol.
verse: I should lye else,
Trust me, extreamly lye Sir.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: Didst thou never wish Olimpia,
It might be thus?

speeches.speaker: Ol.
verse: A thousand times.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: Here take him:
Nay, do not blush: I do not jest; kiss sweetly:
Boy, you kiss faintly Boy; Heaven give you Comfort:
Teach him, he'll quickly learn: there's two Hearts eas'd now.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: You do me too much honour Sir.

speeches.speaker: Duk.
verse: No Archas,
But all I can, I will; can you love me? speak truly.

speeches.speaker: Hon.
verse: Yes Sir, dearly.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: Come hither Viola, can you Love this Man?

speeches.speaker: Viol.
verse: I'll do the best I can Sir.

speeches.speaker: Duk.
verse: Seal it Burris:
We'll all to Church together instantly:
And then a Vie for Boys; stay, bring Borosky.
I had almost forgot that lump of Mischief.
There Archas, take the Enemy to honour,
The Knave to worth: do with him what thou wilt.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: Then to my Sword again; you to your Prayers;
Wash off your Villanies, you feel the Burthen.

speeches.speaker: Bor.
verse: Forgive me 'ere I die, most honest Archas;
'Tis too much honour that I perish thus;
O strike my Faults to kill them that no Memory,
No black and blasted Infamy hereafter—

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: Come, are you ready?

speeches.speaker: Bor.
verse: Yes.

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: And truly penitent, to make your way straight?

speeches.speaker: Bor.
verse: Thus I wash off my Sins

speeches.speaker: Ar.
verse: Stand up, and live then,
And live an honest Man; I scorn Mens ruine:
Take him again. Sir, try him: and believe
This thing will be a perfect Man.

speeches.speaker: Du.
verse: I take him.

speeches.speaker: Bor.
verse: And when I fail those Hopes, Heaven's Hopes fail me.

speeches.speaker: Duk.
verse: You are old: no more Wars Father:
Theodore take you the Charge, be General.

speeches.speaker: The.
verse: All good Bless you.

speeches.speaker: Duk.
verse: And my good Father, you dwell in my Bosom,
From you rise all my good Thoughts: when I would think
And examine Time for one that's fairly Noble,
And the same Man through all the straights of Vertue,
Upon this Silver Book I'll look, and read him.
Now forward merrily to Hymens Rights,
To Joys and Revels, Sports, and he that can
Most honour Archas, is the noblest Man.
